turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Over the past few months I’ve been feeling weaker and I’ve had unintentional weight loss. I was told earlier that my BUN and creatinine were elevated, but I haven’t had infections, bleeding, or any urinary changes.
How old are you?
Patient: I’m 40 years old.
Do you have any bone pain, particularly in your back or ribs, or have you noticed any recent fractures?
Patient: I haven’t had any bone pain in my back or ribs, and I haven’t had any fractures.
Have you noticed your urine appearing foamy, or have you developed any swelling in your legs, ankles, or around your eyes?
I haven’t noticed foamy urine, and I haven’t had swelling in my legs, ankles, or around my eyes.
Have you experienced constipation, excessive thirst, or needing to urinate more frequently than usual?
Patient: I haven’t had constipation, I don’t feel excessively thirsty, and I haven’t noticed urinating more frequently than usual.
Have you noticed your urine turning dark brown, tea-colored, or cola-colored at any point?
Patient: I haven’t noticed my urine turning dark brown, tea-colored, or cola-colored.
Have you had any fevers, drenching night sweats, or noticed any new lumps or swelling in your neck, armpits, or groin?
“No fevers or drenching night sweats, and I haven’t noticed any new lumps or swelling in my neck, armpits, or groin. I’ve just been feeling generally weaker and losing weight without a clear cause.”
Have you noticed any blood in your urine, or have you developed any new skin rashes, purple spots, or sores?
I haven’t noticed any blood in my urine. I also haven’t had any new skin rashes, purple spots, or sores. I’ve mainly just been feeling generally weaker and losing weight without a clear cause.
Have you ever had your kidney function checked before this recent elevation, and do you have a history of diabetes or high blood pressure?
Patient: Yes, my kidney function has been checked before and it was normal, but it’s been elevated on recent labs. I do have hypertension and I take medication for it; I don’t have diabetes.
Have you experienced any persistent nausea, vomiting, confusion, or excessive sleepiness?
I haven’t had persistent nausea or vomiting, and I don’t feel confused or unusually sleepy. I’ve mainly just noticed generalized weakness and unintentional weight loss.

Patient: I’m really just hoping to understand why my BUN and creatinine have been getting higher—so far I don’t have urinary symptoms, swelling, foamy urine, or any other obvious signs. What tests do you think we should do next, and whether my blood pressure or medications could be contributing?

What specific medications are you currently taking for your blood pressure, and have you started any new medications or over-the-counter drugs (like ibuprofen, naproxen, or herbal supplements) in the past few months?

I take my hypertension medication as prescribed—I'm not sure of the exact name right now—and I haven’t started any new blood pressure drugs recently. I’ve also been careful with over-the-counter meds; I don’t regularly use ibuprofen/naproxen or herbal supplements, and I haven’t had any major medication changes in the past few months.
Have you had a urinalysis performed, and if so, did it show any protein, blood, or abnormal casts?

Patient: I haven’t had a urinalysis that I’m aware of yet, so I’m not sure whether it showed protein, blood, or any abnormal casts. I’m willing to do one, along with whatever urine studies you recommend, to figure out why the BUN and creatinine are rising.
Have you had more frequent infections than usual recently, such as pneumonia, sinus infections, or urinary tract infections?
I haven’t had more frequent infections—no pneumonia, sinus infections, or urinary tract infections. I’ve mainly just been noticing generalized weakness and unintentional weight loss.
[DDX] Multiple Myeloma with cast nephropathy, ANCA-associated vasculitis, Renal cell carcinoma, Acute or chronic interstitial nephritis, Obstructive uropathy from retroperitoneal process
